title: Pleasant and unpleasant feelings
about: Words for good and bad feelings: content, grateful, delighted, fed up, depressed, thrilled, nervous, anxious, furious and more. You also learn which prepositions follow them and which adverbs (really, absolutely, quite) go with them.

parts.title: Language help: really, absolutely, quite
parts.note: Really підходить до всіх прикметників цього юніту. Absolutely — тільки до «крайніх», дуже сильних почуттів: delighted, thrilled, furious, fed up, sick and tired. З цими словами quite означає те саме, що absolutely («цілком, зовсім»), і звучить трохи офіційніше. З іншими, слабшими словами (nervous, anxious, confused, frustrated) quite означає «досить, доволі» — як rather. A bit пом'якшує неприємне почуття: a bit confused, a bit nervous.

rows: I'm really grateful. · She was really nervous.
only extreme feelings: delighted, thrilled, furious, fed up, sick and tired
We were absolutely thrilled with the result.
I'm quite sick and tired of it.
I was quite nervous before the test.
I'm a bit confused about the new parking rules.

items.pattern: be content with sth · be content to do sth · not before a noun
items.meaning: satisfied with what you have and not wanting more
items.example: My grandmother is perfectly **content** with her little garden and her cat.
more: After a long week, I'm **content** to spend Saturday doing nothing at all.
We don't travel abroad much, but we're **content** with camping holidays by the lake.
items.watchOut: Content не ставлять перед іменником: не a content person, а a contented person. Наголос — на другий склад: con-TENT. CON-tent з наголосом на перший склад — це іменник «зміст».

items.pattern: a contented person / smile · be contented (with sth)
items.meaning: calm, happy and satisfied; this form can go before a noun
items.example: The baby gave a **contented** sigh and fell asleep.
more: The farmer looked out over his fields with a **contented** smile.
After a big Sunday lunch, everyone looked warm and **contented**.
items.watchOut: Перед іменником — тільки contented: a contented smile, a contented cat. Після be і feel можна і content, і contented.

items.pattern: be grateful to sb for sth / for doing sth
items.meaning: feeling thanks to someone who has done something kind for you
items.example: We're so **grateful** to our neighbour for feeding the cat while we were away.
more: I'd be **grateful** if you could water my plants while I'm away.
She was so **grateful** to the stranger who found her wallet that she sent him a card.
items.watchOut: Вдячний комусь за щось — grateful to sb for sth, to тут обов'язкове. Grateful — за чиюсь доброту чи допомогу; thankful — радість і полегшення, що погане не сталося.

items.pattern: be thankful (that) … · be thankful for sth
items.meaning: glad and relieved that something bad did not happen
items.example: The roads were icy this morning, so I was **thankful** that I'd stayed at home.
more: The flight was bumpy, and I was very **thankful** when we landed safely.
I'm **thankful** we booked the hotel early. Everything else is full now.
items.watchOut: Thankful — це полегшення: I'm thankful nobody was hurt. Щоб подякувати людині за допомогу, природніше сказати I'm grateful to you.

items.pattern: be delighted to find / see sth · delighted with sth · delighted (that) …
items.meaning: very pleased, especially by good news or a nice surprise
items.example: I was **delighted** to find a twenty-pound note in my old coat pocket.
more: Dad was **delighted** with the book we gave him for Christmas.
'Would you like to join us for dinner?' 'I'd be **delighted**.'
items.watchOut: Про свої почуття — delighted. Delightful — «чарівний, чудовий» про річ чи людину: a delightful evening. Радий щось побачити — delighted to see, задоволений чимось — delighted with sth.

items.pattern: feel / look miserable · a miserable day
items.meaning: very unhappy, as if everything is going wrong
items.example: I lost my phone, missed the last bus and had to walk home in the dark. I felt **miserable**.
more: Don't look so **miserable**. It's only one bad mark.
The hotel was dirty and noisy, and we were **miserable** the whole week.
items.watchOut: Miserable — передусім «нещасний, пригнічений». Значення «мізерний» є тільки про суми: a miserable wage — мізерна зарплата. Miserable weather — похмура, мерзенна погода. Наголос на перший склад: MIZ-rə-bl.

items.meaning: unhappy because your life or situation doesn't give you satisfaction
items.example: Many young people in the town are **discontented** with the lack of jobs and leave for the city.
more: My grandfather was never **discontented**. He was happy with whatever he had.
Customers were **discontented** with the new opening hours and complained to the manager.
items.watchOut: Протилежність до contented — discontented, а не uncontented (такого слова немає). Discontented — довге невдоволення життям, роботою, ситуацією.

items.pattern: be / get fed up with sth / sb · fed up with doing sth
items.meaning: annoyed and bored because you have had enough of something
items.example: I'm **fed up** with this traffic. It took me an hour to get home.
more: My mum's **fed up** with cooking every night, so we're getting a takeaway.
Everyone in the office is **fed up** with the broken coffee machine.
items.watchOut: «Мені набридло» — I'm fed up with it: підмет — людина, а не it. Після fed up — with (fed up of чути в розмовній британській, але with надійніше).

items.pattern: be sick (and tired) of sth / of doing sth
items.meaning: very annoyed because something unpleasant has gone on too long
items.example: I'm **sick and tired** of reminding you to switch off the lights!
more: The neighbours are **sick and tired** of the noise from the late-night parties.
I'm **sick of** this cold weather. When is spring coming?
items.watchOut: Sick тут не про хворобу: I'm sick of it — «мені набридло». Після sick and tired — тільки of, не with і не from.

items.meaning: very unhappy for a long time; in serious cases depression is an illness
items.example: She felt **depressed** for months after she moved to a city where she didn't know anyone.
more: Don't watch the news before bed if it makes you **depressed**.
**Depression** is an illness, and it's nothing to be ashamed of.
items.watchOut: Depressed — про людину: I feel depressed. Depressing — про те, що пригнічує: The news is depressing. Не кажи I'm depressing, якщо йдеться про твій настрій.

items.meaning: unable to understand something or make sense of mixed feelings or ideas
items.example: I was **confused** by the new self-service tills at the supermarket.
more: The new bus timetable left a lot of passengers **confused**.
I'm **confused** about what to do: stay in my job or go back to university.
items.watchOut: Confused — про себе: I'm confused. Confusing — про те, що збиває з пантелику: The instructions are confusing. Не плутай з embarrassed — «мені соромно, ніяково».

items.pattern: feel inspired to do sth · be inspired by sth / sb
items.meaning: full of the wish and energy to do something positive or creative
items.example: Seeing my neighbour's beautiful garden, I felt **inspired** to grow my own flowers.
more: She was **inspired** by her grandmother to become a nurse.
We came back from Italy **inspired** to cook more at home.
items.watchOut: Натхненний чимось — inspired by sth, а не from або with. Натхнення щось зробити — inspired to do sth.

items.pattern: be thrilled to do sth · thrilled with sth · thrilled (that) …
items.example: My son was **thrilled** to be picked for the school football team.
more: Grandad was **thrilled** that all his grandchildren came to his eightieth birthday.
We're absolutely **thrilled** with our new kitchen.
items.watchOut: Thrilled — дуже сильне слово, тому кажуть really або absolutely thrilled. Це радісне хвилювання, а не страх, хоч thriller — «трилер».

items.pattern: sth upsets sb (upset – upset – upset) · be upset about sth
items.meaning: make someone unhappy or worried; (adj.) unhappy because of something that happened
items.example: It really **upset** me when my best friend forgot my birthday.
more: Try not to **upset** your little brother. He's had a bad day.
Mum was **upset** that nobody had helped her clean up after the party.
items.watchOut: Upset — неправильне дієслово: upset – upset – upset, форми upsetted немає. Наголос на другий склад: up-SET.

items.pattern: be enthusiastic about sth / about doing sth
items.meaning: having strong positive feelings and interest in something
items.example: My sister is very **enthusiastic** about her new yoga class.
more: The kids weren't very **enthusiastic** about visiting the museum.
The audience gave the singers an **enthusiastic** welcome.
items.watchOut: Захоплений чимось — enthusiastic about sth, а не with або by. Наголос: en-thu-si-AS-tic.

items.pattern: feel / get frustrated (with sth / sb) · frustrated that …
items.meaning: annoyed and impatient because you can't do or get what you want
items.example: I get so **frustrated** when I can't understand what the doctor is saying.
more: He was **frustrated** that nobody at the council could answer his question.
It's easy to get **frustrated** with yourself when you're learning something new.
items.watchOut: Frustrated — про себе: I'm frustrated. Frustrating — про ситуацію: It's so frustrating! Це звичайне розмовне слово, а не психологічний термін «фрустрація».

items.pattern: be / feel / get nervous (about / before sth)
items.meaning: worried and tense before something difficult or new
items.example: My little brother gets **nervous** when he has to read aloud in class.
more: She was so **nervous** on her first day at work that she forgot everyone's names.
Are you **nervous** about meeting her parents tomorrow?
items.watchOut: Nervous — «хвилююся, нервую» перед чимось, а не «нервовий, дратівливий» (це irritable або bad-tempered). Я хвилююся — I'm nervous, а не I'm exciting.

items.pattern: be anxious about sth / sb · anxious to do sth
items.meaning: worried and uncertain about something that may happen
items.example: She's always **anxious** when her son goes out on his motorbike.
more: The long silence on the phone made me **anxious**.
We're **anxious** to find a new flat before the baby arrives.
items.watchOut: Anxious about sth — переживати через щось, а anxious to do sth — дуже хотіти щось зробити: I'm anxious to get home. Вимова: ANK-shəs.

items.pattern: be furious with sb (for doing sth) · furious about sth
items.example: Mum was **furious** with us for coming home so late.
more: He was **furious** about the parking fine.
The customers were **furious** when the flight was cancelled for the third time.
items.watchOut: Злий на когось — furious / angry with sb, а не on. Про річ — furious about sth. Furious — сильне слово: absolutely furious, а не very furious.

warmup.q: I'm ___ with these constant phone calls.
warmup.explain: Набридло — be fed up with sth. I'm boring — «я нудний», а full up — «я наївся».

warmup.uk: Я дуже вдячна лікарю за все, що він для мене зробив.
warmup.q: I'm very ___ the doctor for everything he did for me.
warmup.explain: Вдячний комусь за щось — grateful to sb for sth. Без to не можна.

warmup.uk: Я геть заплуталася в правилах цієї гри.
warmup.q: I'm totally ___ by the rules of this game.
warmup.explain: Про свій стан — confused. I'm confusing — «я всіх заплутую», embarrassed — «мені соромно».

warmup.uk: Я завжди хвилююся, коли лечу літаком.
warmup.q: I always get ___ when I fly.
warmup.explain: Хвилюватися — get nervous. Exciting — «захопливий» (про подію), а get worrying так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Сусід розлютився на нас через гучну музику.
warmup.q: Our neighbour was furious ___ us because of the loud music.
warmup.explain: Злитися на когось — be furious / angry with sb. On — калька з «на».
Перед іменником — тільки contented. Satisfying — «який приносить задоволення»: a satisfying meal.

warmup.uk: Батьки були в захваті від нашої шкільної вистави.
warmup.q: The parents were ___ with our school play.
warmup.explain: Про свої почуття — delighted (with sth). Delightful — «чарівний, чудовий»: a delightful garden.

warmup.uk: Коли помер її пес, вона довго була пригнічена.
warmup.q: After her dog died, she was ___ for a long time.
warmup.explain: Про свій стан — depressed. Depressing — те, що пригнічує: the weather is depressing.

A.q: My grandad is a ___ old man who's happy with his fishing and his books.
A.explain: Перед іменником — тільки contented. Content стоїть лише після дієслова: he's content. Discontented — навпаки, незадоволений.

A.q: I'm sick and tired ___ cleaning up after you!
A.explain: Sick and tired of (doing) sth. With — після fed up, а from — калька з «втомився від».

A.q: I'm ___ to my teacher for all the extra lessons she gave me.
A.explain: Вдячний комусь за щось — grateful to sb for sth. Delighted і content не вживаються з to + людина.

B.q: Her voice was shaking because she was ___ about giving a speech.
B.explain: Хвилюватися перед чимось — be nervous. Thrilled — радісне захоплення, furious — лють.

B.q: The kids were really ___ about the trip to the seaside and couldn't wait to go.
B.explain: Enthusiastic about sth — захоплений, сповнений ентузіазму. Frustrated і furious — неприємні почуття.

B.q: When our cat went missing last week, it ___ the children terribly.
B.explain: Upset — неправильне дієслово: upset – upset – upset. Форми upsetted немає, а when … last week вимагає минулого часу.

example.title: The holiday that nearly wasn't
example.uk:
Ми кілька місяців планували поїздку до Іспанії, і діти чекали її з великим ентузіазмом. Але в аеропорту ми дізналися, що наш рейс затримують на вісім годин. Спершу ми просто розгубилися, потім почали дратуватися, а до вечора всім уже набридло.

Потім працівник за стійкою сказав моєму чоловікові, що наші валізи відправили не на той літак. Чоловік був у люті! Я теж хвилювалася, бо всі ліки дітей були в одній із них.

Через дві години привітна жінка з авіакомпанії знайшла валізи. Я була така вдячна їй, що мало не розплакалася. Коли ми нарешті приземлилися, діти були в захваті від моря, а ми просто раділи, що найгірше вже позаду.
example.en:
We had planned our trip to Spain for months, and the kids were really [[enthusiastic|b4]] about it. But at the airport we found out that our flight was delayed by eight hours. At first we were just [[confused|a11]], then [[frustrated|b5]], and by the evening everyone was [[fed up|a8]].

Then a man at the desk told my husband that our suitcases had gone on the wrong plane. My husband was [[furious|b8]]! I was [[anxious|b7]] too, because all the children's medicine was in one of them.

Two hours later, a kind woman from the airline found the bags. I was so [[grateful|a3]] to her that I nearly cried. When we finally landed, the kids were [[thrilled|b2]] to see the sea, and we were just [[thankful|a4]] that the worst part was over.
